correctness.rationale: For every admissible n-dependent edge-weight choice, the exact q-numerical norm envelope follows from convexity, Perron singular-vector derivatives and the norming subspace at t=0. Comparison of the irreducible singular norm tridiagonal with its central principal block and the unweighted full path proves uniform upper and lower bounds. The n^-2 expansion is uniform on compact t sets, and a rationalized lower bound confines all q_n<1 minimizers to one such set. The c=0 endpoint follows from an ordinary numerical-radius spectral squeeze. Direct finite checker passed 276 assertions; no finite evidence substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: This identifies a sharp crossover curve at the n^-2 scale that is uniform under arbitrary positive, even vanishingly weak, fixed-width end couplings. This perturbation universality is a structural geometric property beyond any calculation for one fixed Jordan matrix or single q; it pinpoints both the classical π²/2 loss and the exact c=π²/2 norm plateau, while showing end defects influence only lower-order terms.
